etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Latin circulatus, past participle of Late Latin circulare (“make circular, encircle”), a later collateral form of circulari (“form a circle (of men) around oneself”), from circulus (“a circle”).

definitions.definition: (intransitive) to move in circles or through a circuit
(transitive) to cause (a person or thing) to move in circles or through a circuit
to move from person to person, as at a party
